# 2026 individual rates used in this engagement

*Citation:* IRC §1(h), §1(j); §1411  
*Status in this library:* in force

For this engagement use: ordinary income marginal rate **37%**; long-term capital gain **20%**; the 3.8% net investment income tax does **not** apply to gain from an active trade or business in which the taxpayer materially participates. Texas has no individual income tax.
# IRC §1060 and Form 8594 — residual method

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §1060; Treas. Reg. §1.1060-1; Form 8594 Instructions  
*Status in this library:* in force

In an applicable asset acquisition, consideration is allocated under the residual method among seven classes in order: I cash; II actively traded personal property; III mark-to-market assets and receivables; IV inventory; V all other assets (equipment, real property); VI section 197 intangibles other than goodwill (including covenants not to compete); VII goodwill and going concern value. Each class is allocated up to fair market value before moving to the next. **Buyer and seller must each file Form 8594 and report consistently** with any written allocation agreement.
# IRC §1245 — gain from dispositions of certain depreciable property

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §1245(a)(1)  
*Status in this library:* in force

If section 1245 property is disposed of, the amount by which the lower of (A) the recomputed basis of the property, or (B) the amount realized, exceeds the adjusted basis of such property **shall be treated as ordinary income**. (Recomputed basis = adjusted basis plus depreciation allowed or allowable.) Such gain is recognized notwithstanding any other provision of this subtitle.
# IRC §1374 — tax imposed on certain built-in gains

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §1374(a), (b), (d)(7)  
*Status in this library:* in force

(a) If for any taxable year beginning in the **recognition period** an S corporation has a net recognized built-in gain, there is imposed a tax (computed under subsection (b)) on the income of such corporation for such taxable year. (b)(1) The tax is the highest corporate rate (**21%**) on the net recognized built-in gain. (d)(7) The recognition period is the **5-year period beginning with the first day of the first taxable year for which the corporation was an S corporation**. Recognized built-in gain on an asset is limited to the asset's built-in gain at the start of the recognition period. The tax paid is treated as a loss sustained by the S corporation (§1366(f)(2)).
# IRC §197 and covenants not to compete

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §197(d)(1)(E); Rev. Rul. 69-643; *Muskat v. United States*, 554 F.3d 183 (1st Cir. 2009)  
*Status in this library:* in force

A covenant not to compete entered into in connection with the acquisition of a trade or business is a section 197 intangible amortizable by the buyer over 15 years. **To the seller, payments for a covenant not to compete are ordinary income** (compensation for refraining from competing), not capital gain. Allocation between a covenant and goodwill must reflect economic reality; the parties' written allocation is binding on them (§1060(a); *Danielson* rule) absent strong proof, and the IRS may challenge it.
# IRC §453 — installment method

*Citation:* 26 U.S.C. §453(a), (b), (i)  
*Status in this library:* in force

Income from an installment sale is taken into account under the installment method (gain recognized proportionately as payments are received), **except** that recapture income under §1245 is recognized in the year of sale regardless of payments (§453(i)), and the method is not available for inventory or for sales of depreciable property to related persons.
# Stock vs asset sale — tax and liability overview

*Citation:* Practitioner summary  
*Status in this library:* in force

Stock (membership-interest) sale: seller recognizes capital gain on the difference between price and stock basis; buyer takes carryover basis in assets (no step-up unless a §338(h)(10)/§336(e) election, which converts the deal to a deemed asset sale with asset-sale consequences to the seller); buyer inherits all liabilities. Asset sale: gain computed asset by asset under the allocation; recapture and covenant payments are ordinary; buyer gets a basis step-up; S corporations within the §1374 recognition period owe entity-level built-in gains tax. Price differences between the two structures typically reflect the buyer's step-up value and assumed liabilities.
